title: planars command operation record list
description: A list of operation records, one per python -m coding command, documenting the relational knowledge Phase 4 of the data layer plan (issue #271) absorbs out of CLAUDE.md's narrative prose: side effects, idempotency, preconditions, which data_dependency_schema facts a command touches and how, what it triggers downstream, and required ordering relative to other commands. Distinct from fact_record.schema.json (the same FACT recorded in multiple places) and precondition_record.schema.json (a shared invariant several commands assume) -- this is per-COMMAND metadata, one record per entry in coding/__main__.py's _COMMANDS table. See SCHEMA.md.

fact.description: A fact id from facts.yaml. Not cross-validated by JSON Schema (drafts can't reference another file's dynamic enum) -- checked by a belt-and-suspenders test instead, same approach as fact_record's authoritative-in-locations check.

role.description: Whether this command reads the fact's current value, writes (changes the authoritative copy or a derived one), or both.

name.description: The flag or sub-behavior distinguishing this mode from the command's default, e.g. '--regen-construction' or '--to-sheet'.

idempotent.description: Same retry-safety meaning as the parent record's idempotent field -- see that field's description.

writes_to_drive.description: Same meaning as the parent record's writes_to_drive field, restated for this mode specifically -- see that field's description. Several commands' Drive-write status genuinely diverges by mode (sync-diagnostics-yaml's default/--from-tsv directions touch only the local YAML/TSV; only --to-sheet writes the live Sheet -- import-planar's default/--to-sheet split the same way), which is exactly why this is a mode field and not only a parent-record one.

mode.description: A full, self-contained override for one named mode of a command whose behavior genuinely diverges by flag -- NOT merged with the parent record's own top-level fields. The parent's top-level side_effects/idempotent/idempotency_note/apply_gate/preconditions/facts_touched describe the command's default invocation only; each mode restates its own values completely, even where they happen to match the default, so nothing has to be reconstructed by inheritance.

id.description: Snake_case form of the CLI command name (hyphens -> underscores), e.g. 'generate_sheets' for 'generate-sheets'. Used to check every entry in coding/__main__.py's _COMMANDS table has a record.

cli_command.description: The exact hyphenated command as typed: 'python -m coding <cli_command>'.

description.description: A one-line, plain-language statement of what the command does.

side_effects.description: What the command creates, writes, or changes when run. A pure reader still gets an entry: 'none (read-only)'.

idempotent.description: Retry-safety, not philosophical purity: given the same external state (nothing else changed since the last run), is running this command a second time equivalent to running it once -- in particular, is it safe to re-run after a failure or an uncertain-completion? Most planars commands can never be 'pure' idempotent in the sense of always producing the same output regardless of when they run, since their whole job is to reflect live Drive/Sheet state that changes constantly -- that is not what this field asks. This is a load-bearing claim: Phases 7 and 8 build recovery logic on top of it, so a wrong 'true' produces recovery that corrupts rather than repairs. Reviewed explicitly, not inferred from the description; where retry-safety genuinely depends on unverified downstream behavior (e.g. a third-party API's tolerance for a repeat call), say so in idempotency_note and default to false rather than assuming true.

idempotency_note.description: Why the idempotent value is true or false -- concrete enough that the claim can be checked, not just asserted. Required even when idempotent is true, since 'true' is the more dangerous claim to get wrong.

apply_gate.description: What gates live writes: the flag name ('--apply'), a fuller description when different modes are gated differently, or null for a command with no live-write concept at all (pure read-only).

preconditions.description: Precondition ids from preconditions.yaml that this command's apply path assumes hold. Empty array if none. Not cross-validated by JSON Schema; checked by a belt-and-suspenders test.

facts_touched.description: Which data_dependency_schema facts this command reads or writes. Empty array if none of the currently-registered facts apply -- not exhaustive by design (see SCHEMA.md's 'don't try to be exhaustive'); grounded in facts.yaml's own cascade/drift_risk text where possible rather than speculative.

cascades_triggered.description: What this command's own run sets off downstream, automatically, as a side effect -- e.g. another command's regeneration step, a notification. Empty array if nothing is triggered.

ordering_constraints.description: Plain-language 'run X before/after Y, because Z' statements naming other commands by cli_command. This is the field that absorbs CLAUDE.md's scattered sequencing prose (--regen-construction bypassing --apply; --split-element before --regen-construction; prune-manifest for retirement but never rename). Empty array if this command has no ordering dependency on any other. Modes are named inline here rather than getting their own ordering_constraints field -- ordering is about sequencing relative to other commands, which stays a whole-command concern even when the command itself has multiple modes.

modes.description: Full overrides for named modes (flags) whose preconditions, facts touched, apply gate, or idempotency genuinely diverge from the command's default invocation, described by this record's own top-level fields. Empty array for a command with no such divergence -- most commands. See the 'mode' $def for what 'override, not merge' means.

writes_to_drive.description: Whether this command's default invocation actually writes to Drive/Sheets/Docs (create, update, share, delete -- not merely read) when its apply_gate is satisfied. Added for Phase 5 unit E (issue #271): coding/provenance.py logs a run only when writes_to_drive is true for the gate that was actually satisfied, so the log records 'which run produced this Drive change' precisely rather than every --apply invocation regardless of what it touched. A command whose Drive-write status is uniform across its whole invocation states it here; a command where it genuinely diverges by mode (sync-diagnostics-yaml, import-planar) restates it per-mode instead -- see the mode $def's own writes_to_drive field. false for a command with no live-write concept at all (pure read-only, e.g. capture-drive-state, integrity-check) and for one whose writes are entirely local (coded_data/ or a local YAML/JSON file, never Drive itself, e.g. sync-diagnostics-yaml's default direction, sync-qualification-hashes).
